From the de-identified open data in `data/open/` (codebook:
`data/open/README.md`; built from the raw jsPsych files by
`analysis/0_deidentify.R`, which only the holder of the raw files runs) to the
derived files every analysis starts from. They are written to `data/`, which is
gitignored:

| file | content |
| --- | --- |
| `data/groups.csv` | who is in the illusion analysis and in which group (Never / Past / Recent), with the screening answers that decided it |
| `data/questionnaires.csv` | AAQ-II, DASS-21 and MEQ-30 scores, for every session with items |
| `data/data_illusiongame.csv` | the Illusion Game test trials of everyone in `groups.csv`, cleaned and scaled: the input of the model in `analysis/server/models.R` |

Render from the repo root (about 15 seconds):

```bash
quarto render analysis/0_preprocessing.qmd
```

The group rules are the manuscript's (Participants section) and reproduce its
43 / 39 / 35 exactly, with one departure decided on 2026-11-02: a control who
typed age 16 is kept as a probable typing error, with age missing, so Never is
44. The trial cleaning follows IllusionGameComputational, the source of the
model's priors, rather than the manuscript. Each section ends with a check that
stops the render if a count changes.

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

# Runs from analysis/ (quarto) or from the repo root (interactively).
repo <- if (dir.exists("server")) ".." else "."
data_path <- function(...) file.path(repo, "data", ...)

participants <- read.csv(data_path("open/participants.csv"))

group_col <- c(Never = "#7a7a75", Past = "#2a78d6", Recent = "#eb6834")
illusions <- c(Ebbinghaus = "Ebbinghaus", MullerLyer = "Müller-Lyer",
               VerticalHorizontal = "Vertical-Horizontal")
theme_igsa <- theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "#ebebe8", linewidth = 0.3),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.justification = "left",
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
    plot.caption = element_text(colour = "#6b6b66", hjust = 0)
  )
```

## Sessions

The open data hold every session of the study's four arms, whatever its later
inclusion. The arm is the experiment's `group` URL parameter: `control` and
`control_T0_bis` are psychedelic-naïve controls, `psychedelic_society` (French)
and `psychedelics_soc_english` are users recruited through psychedelic
societies. The longitudinal arm (`control_T0`, `ketamine_*`, `*_T1`) is not in
the open data.

```{r}
knitr::kable(addmargins(table(Arm = participants$Arm, Language = participants$Session_Language)))
```

`r sum(participants$Completed_IG & participants$Completed_SAT)` of
`r nrow(participants)` sessions completed both tasks;
`r sum(participants$Completed_IG & !participants$Completed_SAT)` have the full
Illusion Game but no self-association task.

## Groups

Each arm ran its own screening (`experiment/demographics.js`). The rules:

- **Eligible:** completed both tasks, and tested by April 2026, the data
  freeze. The manuscript's last session is 2026-04-02; the open data keep the
  month only, and no session falls between that day and May. Three users were
  tested later (May and September 2026); set `freeze <- NA` to include them.
  (A stated age under 18 is handled upstream: the only one, the age-16 control,
  has age missing in the open data, and `0_deidentify.R` stops on any other.)
- **Never:** control arm, answering No to "Have you ever taken a classical
  psychedelic in your life?".
- **Recent:** psychedelic-society arm whose last classic psychedelic was 30
  days ago or less. Days come from the free-text "how many days since your last
  classic psychedelic?" ("18 jours", "3 semaines", "Environ 12 mois"); where it
  cannot be read, from the yes/no "in the last month?" just before it. The
  days rather than the yes/no answer is what reproduces the manuscript: they
  disagree for 7 of 80 users (e.g. "Yes" with 45 or 60 days), and the yes/no
  answer alone gives 43 / 32 instead of 39 / 35.
- **Past:** the same arm, more than 30 days.
- **Out:** controls reporting use, and users reporting experience only with
  non-classic substances, i.e. a lifetime frequency of "Never" *and* a
  non-classic ("Other") last substance. Either alone is not enough: S115 says
  "Never" but took ayahuasca, S060 took "Other" last but classics 11-50 times,
  and the manuscript kept both.

```{r}
freeze <- "2026-04" # last month included (YYYY-MM)
control_arms <- c("control", "control_T0_bis")
user_arms <- c("psychedelic_society", "psychedelics_soc_english")

# "14", "18 jours", "3 semaines", "Environ 12 mois", "4 months ago", "5 ans"
parse_days <- function(x) {
  s <- tolower(trimws(x))
  m <- regmatches(s, regexec("^(?:environ |about )?([0-9]+(?:[.,][0-9]+)?) *(.*)$", s, perl = TRUE))
  vapply(m, function(h) {
    if (length(h) != 3) return(NA_real_)
    n <- as.numeric(sub(",", ".", h[2]))
    unit <- h[3]
    if (unit == "" || grepl("^(jour|day|à peu|a peu)", unit)) return(n)
    if (grepl("^(semaine|week)", unit)) return(7 * n)
    if (grepl("^(mois|month)", unit)) return(30 * n)
    if (grepl("^(an|year)", unit)) return(365 * n)
    NA_real_
  }, numeric(1))
}

df <- participants
df$Days <- parse_days(df$Psychedelics_DaysAgo)
recent <- ifelse(!is.na(df$Days), df$Days <= 30, df$Psychedelics_LastMonth %in% "Yes")
only_non_classic <- df$Psychedelics_Frequency %in% "Never" & df$Experience_Substance %in% "Other"
df$Group <- ifelse(
  df$Arm %in% control_arms,
  ifelse(df$Psychedelics_Ever %in% "No", "Never", "out: control reporting use"),
  ifelse(df$Arm %in% user_arms,
         ifelse(only_non_classic, "out: non-classic substances only",
                ifelse(recent, "Recent", "Past")),
         "out: not in this study's arms")
)
df$Group[!(df$Completed_IG & df$Completed_SAT)] <- "out: protocol not completed"
df$Group[!is.na(freeze) & df$Session_Month > freeze] <- "out: after the data freeze"

excluded <- startsWith(df$Group, "out")
included <- df[!excluded, ]
included$Group <- factor(included$Group, levels = c("Never", "Past", "Recent"))

groups <- df[!excluded, c("Participant", "Group", "Arm", "Session_Month", "Psychedelics_Ever",
                          "Psychedelics_LastMonth", "Psychedelics_DaysAgo", "Days",
                          "Psychedelics_Frequency", "Experience_Substance")]
write.csv(groups[order(groups$Group, groups$Participant), ], data_path("groups.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

Where the yes/no answer and the days disagree, the days win:

```{r}
odd <- !is.na(df$Days) & !is.na(df$Psychedelics_LastMonth) &
  (df$Days <= 30) != (df$Psychedelics_LastMonth == "Yes") & df$Group %in% c("Recent", "Past")
knitr::kable(df[odd, c("Participant", "Group", "Psychedelics_LastMonth", "Psychedelics_DaysAgo")],
             row.names = FALSE)
```

Excluded:

```{r}
knitr::kable(df[excluded, c("Participant", "Arm", "Session_Month", "Group")], row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
counts <- table(included$Group)
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(counts, responseName = "N"), col.names = c("Group", "N"))
# The manuscript's 43 / 35 / 39, plus the age-16 control in Never.
stopifnot(identical(as.vector(counts[c("Never", "Past", "Recent")]), c(44L, 35L, 39L)))
```

## Sample

The groups differ in more than psychedelic use: the controls are younger,
mostly students, and less than half are native speakers of the session's
language. These are reported in the paper, not adjusted for (see `AGENTS.md`,
"Age and the other group differences").

```{r}
pct <- function(x) sprintf("%d (%.0f%%)", sum(x, na.rm = TRUE), 100 * mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))
education <- c("High school", "Bachelor", "Master", "Doctorate", "Other")
education <- education[education %in% included$Education]
describe <- function(g) {
  age <- g$Age
  c(
    "N" = nrow(g),
    "Age, median (range)" = sprintf("%g (%g-%g)", median(age, na.rm = TRUE), min(age, na.rm = TRUE), max(age, na.rm = TRUE)),
    "Age, mean (SD)" = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(age, na.rm = TRUE), sd(age, na.rm = TRUE)),
    "Age missing" = sum(is.na(age)),
    "Women" = pct(g$Sex == "Female"),
    "Students" = pct(g$Student == "Yes"),
    "Native speakers" = pct(g$Language_Level == "Native"),
    "Session in English" = pct(g$Session_Language == "English"),
    setNames(sapply(education, function(e) pct(g$Education == e)), paste("Education:", education)),
    "Past diagnosis" = pct(g$Diagnosis_Past == "Yes"),
    "Current diagnosis" = pct(g$Diagnosis_Current == "Yes"),
    "Meditates weekly" = pct(g$Meditation == "Yes")
  )
}
knitr::kable(sapply(split(included, included$Group), describe))
```

Ages by group:

```{r}
included$Age_Band <- cut(included$Age, c(-Inf, 25, 30, 50, Inf),
                         labels = c("<= 25", "26-30", "31-50", "> 50"))
knitr::kable(addmargins(table(Group = included$Group, Age = included$Age_Band, useNA = "ifany"), 2))
```

```{r}
ggplot(included[!is.na(included$Age), ], aes(Age, Group, colour = Group)) +
```

## Questionnaires

Items are stored as jsPsych's 0-based index of the chosen label
(`experiment/questionnaires.js` has the labels and wording). None of the three
instruments has a reverse-keyed item, and in every one the first label is the
lowest anchor, so a higher index is more of what the scale measures. The
scoring follows the manuscript:

- **AAQ-II** (7 items, "never true" to "always true"): the sum, with the items
  on the published 1-7 scale (the stored 0-6 plus one), so the range is 7-49
  and the published cut-offs apply. Higher is less psychological flexibility.
- **DASS-21** (21 items, 0 "did not apply to me at all" to 3 "applied to me
  very much"): the mean of the 7 items of each subscale (Depression, Anxiety,
  Stress), on 0-3, and the total as the mean of the three. (The conventional
  severity scores are the subscale sums doubled, i.e. 14 times these means.)
- **MEQ-30** (30 items, 0 "none, not at all" to 5 "extreme"; users only, about
  their last classic psychedelic experience): the mean of the items of each
  of the four Barrett et al. (2015) factors (Mystical, 15 items; Positive mood,
  6; Transcendence of time and space, 6; Ineffability, 3), and the total as the
  mean of all 30. `MEQ_Complete` flags a "complete mystical experience": at
  least 60% of the maximum (a mean of 3) on all four factors.

**Missing items.** A scale is scored when at most one of its items is missing,
as the mean of the answered items (times the number of items for the AAQ-II
sum); with more missing it is `NA`. A total is `NA` when any of its parts is.
`*_Missing` counts the missing items per instrument.

```{r}
items <- function(pattern) participants[grep(pattern, names(participants))]

# Every stored item is an integer index within the label range.
check_items <- function(x, max_index) {
  v <- unlist(x)
  stopifnot(all(v == round(v), na.rm = TRUE), all(v >= 0, na.rm = TRUE), all(v <= max_index, na.rm = TRUE))
}
check_items(items("^AAQ_"), 6)
check_items(items("^DASS_"), 3)
check_items(items("^MEQ_"), 5)
stopifnot(ncol(items("^AAQ_")) == 7, ncol(items("^DASS_")) == 21, ncol(items("^MEQ_")) == 30)

score <- function(x, max_missing = 1, offset = 0) {
  m <- rowMeans(x + offset, na.rm = TRUE)
  m[rowSums(is.na(x)) > max_missing] <- NA
  m
}

q <- participants[c("Participant", "Arm")]
q$Group <- as.character(included$Group)[match(q$Participant, included$Participant)]

q$AAQ <- 7 * score(items("^AAQ_"), offset = 1)
q$AAQ_Missing <- rowSums(is.na(items("^AAQ_")))

for (s in c("Depression", "Anxiety", "Stress")) q[[paste0("DASS_", s)]] <- score(items(paste0("^DASS_", s, "_")))
q$DASS_Total <- rowMeans(q[c("DASS_Depression", "DASS_Anxiety", "DASS_Stress")])
q$DASS_Missing <- rowSums(is.na(items("^DASS_")))

for (s in c("Mystical", "PositiveMood", "Transcendence", "Ineffability")) q[[paste0("MEQ_", s)]] <- score(items(paste0("^MEQ_", s, "_")))
q$MEQ_Total <- score(items("^MEQ_"))
q$MEQ_Complete <- as.logical(rowSums(q[paste0("MEQ_", c("Mystical", "PositiveMood", "Transcendence", "Ineffability"))] >= 3) == 4)
q$MEQ_Missing <- rowSums(is.na(items("^MEQ_")))

write.csv(q, data_path("questionnaires.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

How many sessions each instrument scores, and what the missing-item rule
does:

```{r}
has_items <- function(pattern) rowSums(!is.na(items(pattern))) > 0
rule <- data.frame(
  Instrument = c("AAQ-II", "DASS-21", "MEQ-30"),
  "With items" = c(sum(has_items("^AAQ_")), sum(has_items("^DASS_")), sum(has_items("^MEQ_"))),
  "Scored" = c(sum(!is.na(q$AAQ)), sum(!is.na(q$DASS_Total)), sum(!is.na(q$MEQ_Total))),
  "Prorated" = c(sum(!is.na(q$AAQ) & q$AAQ_Missing == 1),
                                  sum(!is.na(q$DASS_Total) & q$DASS_Missing > 0),
                                  sum(!is.na(q$MEQ_Total) & q$MEQ_Missing == 1)),
  "Not scored (items missing)" = c(sum(has_items("^AAQ_") & is.na(q$AAQ)),
                                   sum(has_items("^DASS_") & is.na(q$DASS_Total)),
                                   sum(has_items("^MEQ_") & is.na(q$MEQ_Total))),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(rule)
```

Internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha, sessions with every item of the
scale):

```{r}
alpha <- function(x) {
  x <- x[stats::complete.cases(x), ]
  k <- ncol(x)
  c(alpha = k / (k - 1) * (1 - sum(apply(x, 2, stats::var)) / stats::var(rowSums(x))), n = nrow(x))
}
scales <- list(
  "AAQ-II" = "^AAQ_", "DASS-21 total" = "^DASS_", "DASS Depression" = "^DASS_Depression_",
  "DASS Anxiety" = "^DASS_Anxiety_", "DASS Stress" = "^DASS_Stress_", "MEQ-30 total" = "^MEQ_",
  "MEQ Mystical" = "^MEQ_Mystical_", "MEQ Positive mood" = "^MEQ_PositiveMood_",
  "MEQ Transcendence" = "^MEQ_Transcendence_", "MEQ Ineffability" = "^MEQ_Ineffability_"
)
knitr::kable(t(sapply(scales, function(p) alpha(items(p)))), digits = c(2, 0))
```

Scores of the included participants, by group (median [first, third
quartile]; the MEQ-30 is users only):

```{r}
score_cols <- c("AAQ", "DASS_Depression", "DASS_Anxiety", "DASS_Stress", "DASS_Total",
                "MEQ_Mystical", "MEQ_PositiveMood", "MEQ_Transcendence", "MEQ_Ineffability", "MEQ_Total")
qi <- q[!is.na(q$Group), ]
qi$Group <- factor(qi$Group, levels = names(group_col))
summarise_scores <- function(g) {
  sapply(score_cols, function(s) {
    v <- g[[s]][!is.na(g[[s]])]
    if (length(v) == 0) return("")
    sprintf("%.1f [%.1f, %.1f] (n = %d)", median(v), quantile(v, 0.25), quantile(v, 0.75), length(v))
  })
}
knitr::kable(sapply(split(qi, qi$Group), summarise_scores))
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5

long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(score_cols, function(s) {
  data.frame(Group = qi$Group, Scale = s, Score = qi[[s]])
}))
long <- long[!is.na(long$Score), ]
long$Scale <- factor(long$Scale, levels = score_cols)

ggplot(long, aes(Group, Score, colour = Group)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.15, width = 0.5) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, height = 0, alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +

```

## Illusion Game trials

One row per test trial (practice excluded), for every participant in
`groups.csv`, with the predictors the model uses. RT goes from ms to seconds,
which cogmod requires.

**Cleaning** follows IllusionGameComputational (`0_preprocessing.qmd` there),
the source of the priors, rather than the manuscript: the model's outlier
component takes the stray fast and slow responses, so only the impossible ones
go.

- RT <= 0 or RT >= 6 s.
- A participant x illusion x block whose errors on *facilitating* trials reach
  1/3. There the illusion points to the right answer, so an engaged participant
  is near-perfect however sensitive to the illusion they are, and guessing or
  reversed instructions show up as 1/2 or ~1 errors.

**Predictors**, both on [-1, 1], scaled by the task's stimulus grid (the same
for every participant), not by the data, so that a subset cannot change the
units:

- `Illusion_Strength`, signed: + conflicting (pushes towards the error), -
  facilitating; +-1 is the strongest illusion shown. 0 (no illusion) is between
  the grid's +-0.1. As in every Illusion Game file, the sign of the strength
  alone says which way the illusion pushes, whatever the side of the
  difference: errors by sign in the controls are 1-6% when negative, 34-45%
  when positive. There is no strength-0 trial.
- `Task_Difficulty`, from |difference|: +1 the smallest difference shown
  (hardest), -1 the largest (easiest).

This is IllusionGameComputational's transformation (`Illusion_StrengthZ`,
`Illusion_DifferenceZ`) over this task's narrower grid, with the difference
flipped so that the name reads the right way round. The units are therefore
not the same as there.

```{r}
trials <- read.csv(data_path("open/illusiongame.csv"))
trials <- trials[trials$Participant %in% groups$Participant & trials$Block != "Practice", c(
  "Participant", "Illusion_Type", "Illusion_Difference", "Illusion_Strength", "Block", "Trial", "RT", "Error"
)]
n <- table(factor(trials$Participant, levels = groups$Participant))
if (any(n != 480)) stop(paste(names(n)[n != 480], collapse = ", "), ": not 480 test trials", call. = FALSE)
trials$RT <- trials$RT / 1000
trials <- merge(trials, groups[c("Participant", "Group")], by = "Participant")

# Cleaning
n0 <- nrow(trials)
trials <- trials[!is.na(trials$RT) & trials$RT > 0 & trials$RT < 6, ]
n_rt <- n0 - nrow(trials)

trials$Illusion_Effect <- ifelse(trials$Illusion_Strength > 0, "Conflicting", "Facilitating")
block <- paste(trials$Participant, trials$Illusion_Type, trials$Block)
fac <- trials$Illusion_Effect == "Facilitating"
fac_error <- tapply(trials$Error[fac], block[fac], mean)
bad <- names(fac_error)[fac_error >= 1 / 3]
n_block <- sum(block %in% bad)
trials <- trials[!block %in% bad, ]

# Predictors
grid <- data.frame(
  Illusion_Type = c("Ebbinghaus", "MullerLyer", "VerticalHorizontal"),
  Strength_Max = c(1.5, 30, 45),
  Difference_Min = c(0.05, 0.045, 0.03),
  Difference_Max = c(0.5, 0.45, 0.3)
)
g <- grid[match(trials$Illusion_Type, grid$Illusion_Type), ]
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(g$Strength_Max),
  abs(trials$Illusion_Strength) <= g$Strength_Max + 1e-6,
  abs(trials$Illusion_Difference) >= g$Difference_Min - 1e-6,
  abs(trials$Illusion_Difference) <= g$Difference_Max + 1e-6
)
trials$Illusion_Strength_Raw <- trials$Illusion_Strength
trials$Illusion_Strength <- trials$Illusion_Strength_Raw / g$Strength_Max
trials$Task_Difficulty <- 1 - 2 * (abs(trials$Illusion_Difference) - g$Difference_Min) /
  (g$Difference_Max - g$Difference_Min)

trials <- trials[order(trials$Participant, trials$Block, trials$Illusion_Type, trials$Trial), c(
  "Participant", "Group", "Illusion_Type", "Block", "Trial",
  "Illusion_Difference", "Illusion_Strength_Raw", "Illusion_Effect",
  "Illusion_Strength", "Task_Difficulty", "RT", "Error"
)]
write.csv(trials, data_path("data_illusiongame.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

The stimulus grid, in each illusion's units:

```{r}
knitr::kable(grid)
```

`r format(nrow(trials), big.mark = ",")` trials of
`r length(unique(trials$Participant))` participants remain: `r n_rt` trials
were removed on RT and `r n_block` in `r length(bad)` blocks on facilitating
errors.

```{r}
removed <- do.call(rbind, strsplit(bad, " "))
if (length(bad)) knitr::kable(data.frame(Participant = removed[, 1], Illusion = removed[, 2], Block = removed[, 3],
                                         "Facilitating errors" = round(fac_error[bad], 2), check.names = FALSE),
                              row.names = FALSE)
stopifnot(nrow(trials) == 55937, length(unique(trials$Participant)) == 118)
```

What the cleaned trials look like, before any model: the error rate and the
median RT at each strength of the grid, per group and illusion.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5

cells <- aggregate(cbind(Error = trials$Error, RT = trials$RT),
                   by = trials[c("Group", "Illusion_Type", "Illusion_Strength")],
                   FUN = function(x) c(mean = mean(x), median = median(x)))
raw <- rbind(
  data.frame(cells[1:3], Measure = "Error rate", Value = cells$Error[, "mean"]),
  data.frame(cells[1:3], Measure = "Median RT (s)", Value = cells$RT[, "median"])
)
raw$Group <- factor(raw$Group, levels = names(group_col))
raw$Illusion_Type <- factor(illusions[raw$Illusion_Type], levels = illusions)

ggplot(raw, aes(Illusion_Strength, Value, colour = Group)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "#9a9a95", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(size = 1.2) +
  facet_grid(Measure ~ Illusion_Type, scales = "free_y", switch = "y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = group_col) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(-1, 0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Illusion strength (scaled)", y = NULL, colour = NULL,
       title = "Cleaned trials per group",
       caption = "Each point pools every trial of the group at that strength, across task difficulty.\nStrength: + pushes towards the error (conflicting), - towards the right answer (facilitating).") +
  theme_igsa + theme(strip.placement = "outside")
```

## Self-association trials

Not built yet. `data/open/selfassociation.csv` holds every trial of the 125
sessions that reached the task; the cleaning rules of the self-association
paper are still to be decided, and the section that writes
`data/data_selfassociation.csv` belongs here once they are.
